audit.page: Operator process: fleet, thread, approvals, inbox, signin, confirm, states
audit.method: Chromium 155 headless driven with puppeteer-core running the skill's probes.js unchanged (collect + interactive phase), with supplementary focus-cover, clip and overlap probes. The chrome-devtools MCP browser was unavailable (profile locked by another session).
changedSincePreviousAudit: app.css (States sheet .pair__cols container query moved after its base rule; .notice__actions .btn may wrap)
scopeNotes: Level A + AA only (55 criteria). AAA not assessed. 4.1.1 Parsing excluded (removed in WCAG 2.2).
Seven screens audited as one process, each in light and dark, at 1280x800, 640x400 (200%) and 320x256 (400%), plus 320x568, 400x300 and 900x700 where layouts change.
Only app.css and DESIGN.md differ from final-773e1c5; the full sweep was re-run to catch regressions.
Text spacing was applied with a constructable stylesheet because the CSP (style-src 'self') blocks the <style> element probes.js injects.
chrome-devtools MCP not used: its profile was held by Chromium from another running MCP session. Landmarks read from the DOM; HTML unchanged since final-773e1c5 where the MCP tree confirmed them.
No screen reader or speech-input software was run; semantics verified in the accessibility tree.
Not sampled in depth: diff.html, catalog.html, index.html, thread-2..thread-7 (titles, cross-page consistency, and catalog .surfs reflow only).
final-763cbac/ is a read-only generated snapshot: make any fixes in the generator source, not in that folder.

summary.note: Counts cover the 55 Level A + AA criteria and match the coverage table in the HTML report. No failures. The 1.4.10 failure from final-773e1c5 is fixed and no regressions were found. Conformance can be claimed once 2.2.1 (backend time limits) is confirmed; not verified with assistive technology.

needsReview.title: Timing Adjustable
needsReview.whatToReview: Approval expiry ("expires 19:30 CST", "expires 16:30 CST") and session expiry (the "Session expired" sign-in state) in the product: can the operator turn off, adjust or extend each limit with at least 20 seconds' warning, or does an exception (essential, real-time, longer than 20 hours) apply?
needsReview.whyOpen: This prototype shows both limits but runs neither; their lengths come from the backend. The 750 ms arming delay and 3 s cooldown are safety holds, not time limits on the user.
needsReview.howToConfirm: Leave an approval open near its expiry and leave a session idle. Pass if a warning gives at least 20 seconds and a simple way to extend (at least 10 times), or the limit is adjustable, off, essential, or longer than 20 hours. Fail if it expires silently.

advisories.note: Comfortable sizing at 320 px: header, main and footer are 328 px wide in a 320 px viewport; the right 8 px is clipped (pre-existing).
Inbox drawer open with a tooltip showing: one Escape closes the drawer and the tooltip comes back (focus moves to main and re-enables tips); a second Escape hides it.
Tooltips linger 400 ms (--dur-tip) after focus leaves; rapid Tab at 320x256 can briefly cover most of the next focused control (Cancel, Confirm).
While a request waits below 60rem the Workspace menu button is live but does nothing (sidebar is inert); the skip link targets the inert main.
The alertdialog's aria-describedby points at a region with aria-label "Request details", so its description is that label rather than the request text.

With WCAG text spacing: a.tier.tier--b "Human Inbox 3" runs 4 px past a 320 px viewport (right border cut, text intact); sidebar a.pages__link "Confirm gate" label runs 6 px past its current-page highlight. No content lost (pre-existing).
